documents.title: Doc 69 - Infringement - Car 16 - Left the track and gained a lasting advantage
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 16 - Left the track and gained a lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 16 left the track and gained a lasting advantage
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: 5 second time penalty.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video and in-car video evidence. The Stewards have determined that both cars entered turn 4 with excessive speed and therefore neither would have been able to make the corner on track, as demonstrated by the fact that car 44 which was on the inside, had to go off track to make the corner. Car 16 was therefore not entitled to claim the corner due to the excessive entry speed. The driver then completed an overtake whilst off track and accordingly this warrants a penalty. The baseline penalty guideline is 10 seconds however in mitigation is the fact that car 44 was also off track on the inside of car 16 and this occurred early in the first lap.

documents.title: Doc 65 - Infringement - Car 30 - Changes made during Parc Ferme
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 30 - Changes made during Parc Ferme

details.competitor: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
details.fact: The setup of the suspension has been changed while under parc fermé. The team continued to work on the car beyond the covers-on time. The following Power Unit elements have been used: 5th Engine (ICE) 5th Turbocharger (TC) 5th Exhaust Set (EXH) 7th Power Unit Ancillary Component (PU-ANC) All Power Unit elements were replaced without the approval of the FIA Technical Delegate during parc fermé.
details.infringement: Breaches of Articles B3.4.3, B3.5.3 and B3.5.4 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: Required to start the Race from the pit lane.
details.reason: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team changed the setup of the suspension of Car 30 under parc fermé before the start of the Race, without the approval of the Technical Delegate. This is not accordance with Article B3.5.4 of the FIA F1 Regulations. In addition, the change of setup is not in accordance with Article B3.5.3 of the FIA F1 Regulations. Car 30 is therefore required to start the Race from pit lane as per Article B3.5.3a of the FIA F1 Regulations. Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team continued to work on the car beyond the covers-on time which is a breach of Article B3.4.3 of the FIA F1 Regulations. Car 30 is therefore required to start the Race from pit lane as per Article B3.5.3a of the FIA F1 Regulations for this infringement too. The replacement of the Power Unit elements listed above would additionally result in a cumulative grid position penalty of 40 places. Furthermore, Car 30 had previously received a one grid position penalty at this Event (Document 34). The Stewards determine that these grid position penalties are absorbed by the requirement for Car 30 to start the Race from the pit lane and will therefore be considered served.

documents.title: Doc 57 - Infringement - Car 30 - Technical nonconformity
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 30 - Technical nonconformity

details.competitor: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
details.fact: Car 30 did not comply with with the requirements of Articles C5.12.6 and C5.12.7 of the F1 Regulations
details.infringement: Breach of Articles C5.12.6 and C5.12.7 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: Car 30 is disqualified from the results of the Provisional Qualifying Classifications.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the team representatives of Car 30 (Liam Lawson), the driver, the Single Seater Sporting Director and members of the FIA Technical team including the FIA Technical Delegate. Evidence submitted, which was accepted by all parties present, showed that after the control line at the end of his fastest lap in Q2, the driver did not lift off the power immediately. This resulted in the rate of reduction of MGUK deployment required to achieve the regulated “step down”, not being achieved. The team argued that this did not provide any performance advantage however it is clear that non-compliance with the Technical Regulations is not excused if no performance advantage is gained. Further, these regulations require that a car must comply with them at all times during an event. The Stewards note in particular that the team self-disclosed the breach however there are a multitude of precedents that require us, despite all mitigating circumstances, to impose a penalty of Disqualfication where a car does not comply with the Technical Regulations.

documents.title: Doc 50 - Decision - Qualifying SC2-SC1 Times

details.fact: The F1 Cars below exceeded the 1:38.0 time limit between the Safety Car lines.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article B1.8.5 of the FIA F1 Regulations and Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code (non-compliance with the Race Director’s Competition Notes, item 1, document 8).
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards thoroughly reviewed Marshalling/Positioning data and timing data. All drivers concerned stayed at or above speeds necessary to stay below 1:38.0 around the vast majority of the circuit. However, in all cases the Stewards determined that the drivers took appropriate actions to not impede other drivers, and in all cases, they slowed down significantly to allow other drivers to pass while giving those drivers a clear track. The Stewards therefore determine that all drivers concerned did not drive “unnecessarily slowly”, and that they were above the maximum time because they took appropriate steps, and we therefore take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 41 - Infringement - Car 6 - Misconduct
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 6 - Misconduct

details.fact: The driver and a Paddock guest appeared to have an interaction in the Paddock prior to the start of FP1.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.l of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Driver: Formal warning.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 6 (Isack Hadjar) and the team representative and reviewed video evidence. The driver stated that he was running late for FP1 and had stopped to have a photograph with a young fan, when he was approached by a Paddock guest in an aggressive manner. One security person was walking behind him and was unable to intervene and prevent what was tantamount to an invasion of the driver’s private space. The driver initially resisted the move by placing his hand on the waist of the guest, holding him at bay, then the driver pushed him aside with his open right hand. This latter action by the driver is regarded as a breach of the regulations however in mitigation of penalty the stewards considered the following matters (in accordance with the guidelines provided in Appendix B of the FIA International Sporting Code): a) The driver was reacting to an uninvited and rather aggressive action by another person b) The driver was endeavouring to make his way to the start of FP1 through a congested area c) The driver did not have sufficient security present d) The guest was invading his personal space without his consent. e) The general issue drivers have experienced moving through the Paddock

documents.title: Doc 34 - Infringement - Car 30 - Turn 14 incident with Car 3
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 30 - Turn 14 incident with Car 3

details.competitor: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
details.fact: Cars 3 and 30 engaged in a series of moves on the entry to turn 12 through to the apex of turn 14.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 e) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A drop of one grid position for the next race in which the driver competes. One penalty point is imposed, making a total of 4 for the 12 month period.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 3 (Max Verstappen), the driver of Car 30 (Liam Lawson), team representatives and reviewed video evidence. On the approach to turn 12 car 3 was on a preparation lap and car 30 was on a cool down lap preparing for another push lap. The drivers of both cars behaved in a manner that was considered unacceptable by the Stewards particularly in view of the warning that had been given at the Team Managers meeting earlier this day. Both drivers admitted the moves were unnecessary and “clumsy”. Noting that there had been similar incidents this year of actions between drivers in Free Practice, the Stewards have decided to escalate the penalty from that of a formal warning to a grid position penalty particularly in view of the warning that had been provided at the Team Managers meeting and consistent with other incidents involving contact between the cars in Free Practice in previous years.

documents.title: Doc 32 - Infringement - Car 5 - Covering components
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 5 - Covering components

details.fact: The floor of Car 5 was transported by team personnel from one side of the garage to the other whilst covered by a large sheet. In addition, team personnel obstructed the view of Car 5 using another sheet while mechanics were working underneath the car.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B3.3.1 of the FIA Formula One Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: The competitor (Audi Revolut F1 Team) is fined €5,000.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the Team Representative, the FIA Techincal Delegate and reviewed video evidence. The Team Representative recognised the breach and explained that the principal reason for the infringement was the particular configuration of the garages allocated to the Competitor at this Event. The two garages used by the Competitor are separated by a garage occupied by other personnel. As a result, the floor had to be transported through an area visible to third parties, which led the Competitor to cover it while moving it between its two garages. While the Stewards acknowledge the particular circumstances explained by the Competitor, these do not constitute an exception to the requirements of Article B3.3.1. Furthermore, team personnel also obstructed the view of Car 5 using another sheet while mechanics were working underneath the car. The Stewards therefore determine that the Competitor was in breach of Article B3.3.1 of the FIA Formula One Sporting Regulations.

documents.title: Doc 22 - Infringement - Car 98 - Released in an unsafe condition
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 98 - Released in an unsafe condition

details.fact: Car 98 was released with a cooling fan still attached to the intake of the right radiator.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.6.2b.i of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: The competitor (Audi Revolut F1 Team) is fined €7,500.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the team representative and reviewed video evidence. The team representative explained that on noticing that the cooling fan was still attached, he checked with his engineers to ascertain if it was safe to continue the lap and was advised by them that it was. The team then instructed the driver to pit, and it was confirmed the driver was unaware of the issue. Although the fan did not fall off the car (as was the case of a car in Australia this year) there was the possibility it could have. Accordingly a penalty similar to that applied to Car 12 in Australia, was applied.
